title: Growing up speaking Creole
summary: The family spoke Creole, which was looked down on as broken French; stepfather sang in it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I see. What language did you grow up speaking, by the way? Did you use it? Well, my father and my mother was Creole, you know what I mean?

Practically, we all grew up in Creole. Which they didn't want you to learn that, because they called it, said it was a broken French. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. And just grew up with it. Did anybody around your house sing songs in Creole? Or? Well, my daddy used to, my stepfather. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm .
Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . and Panuska Fernandez. He'd lived till the age of 109 or 10 like that. In fact, he outlived the old man.
What sort of songs did they sing? Do you remember any of them? Did they sing in Creole?
I couldn't remember this that long. I was quite a youngster. I was in the neighborhood, say about 10, 11 years old.
